chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We do not count a man as a believer until he is obedient to and desirous of all our affairs. Indeed, among the obedience to our affairs and desiring it is piety (war'). So adorn yourselves with it, may Allah have mercy on you, and inflict hardship on our enemies with it, may Allah invigorate you.

key_terms.يَرْحَمْكُمُ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on you

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that true faith (Iman) is not merely nominal but requires active, wholehearted adherence to the Imam's guidance, with piety (War') serving as the essential manifestation of this devotion. This definition underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inseparability of belief and practical observance, linking spiritual purity directly to communal strength and divine mercy. The exhortation to 'adorn' oneself with piety highlights its role as both a personal spiritual shield and a means of consolidating authority against opponents.
